passage:
At the agency's office, Yusuf slid a folder across the table. "Sign today or the rate goes up." Divyansh noticed that the payment date they had promised out loud was missing from the pages, and there was a fee he had not heard of. "Please put both in writing," he said. Yusuf refused, and Divyansh picked up his bag and left.

It was an older mistake that still stung. Months earlier he had signed a co-working agreement without reading it properly, and now the exit terms were tighter than he remembered. He felt foolish. He took it to Minakshi, a lawyer, who went through the clauses. "In plain words, this one means you pay for the whole year if you leave early." She explained the risks, then added, "It's your decision. I can tell you what I see." Together they drafted a request to amend the agreement.

The co-working owner's reply came within the hour, and it was hot. He was accused of breaking the terms and threatened with legal action. Divyansh took a breath, reread the agreement, gathered the emails and wrote a calm reply that stuck to dates and clauses. At the end he suggested a mediator. He did not answer the last angry call.

qa.q: What was missing from the pages Yusuf pushed Divyansh to sign?
qa.a: The payment date promised out loud was missing, and there was a fee he had not heard of.

qa.q: How did Divyansh's approach with Yusuf's rushed folder differ from the way he dealt with the co-working agreement?
qa.a: With Yusuf he insisted the terms be in writing and walked away when refused. With the co-working agreement he had already signed without reading, so he brought it to Minakshi and then asked to amend it in writing.

qa.q: What was Divyansh feeling when he realised the exit terms were tighter than he remembered?
qa.a: He felt foolish and regretful, as he had signed without reading properly.

qa.q: What could Divyansh do if the co-working owner keeps threatening action?
qa.a: He could keep replies calm and in writing, keep his emails and proofs, and ask Minakshi or a mediator for help before it escalates.

grounding: One professional faces a pushy deal, an old unfavourable signature, a lawyer's plain-language help and an angry counterparty in the same contract story.
